idea: The lander is half the ad: 24 proven advertorial archetypes, each paired with its live ad, ready to model.
sequencing: Hook: 24 lander formats, found in 10 minutes.
The 24 pairs: breaking news → myth-bust, each with ad + URL.
Bonus: 200+ more on the board.
Send-off: "Enjoy and print."
formatting: Long directory post: format name + lander URL + ad link, repeated 24 times. Reference-doc style.
why_it_works: Each entry is a complete stealable unit (format + live proof + ad), so the post functions as 24 swipe files in one.
what_to_steal: The ad→lander pairing discipline: for LC's bundle-picker and offer ads, always study the destination page as part of the creative — a bundle picker ad dying on a generic PDP is a lander problem, not a creative problem.

product: commentary — no product (offer case study; brand not named in file)
hook: "We changed our offer and got a $20 better AOV with roughly the same CVR..."
body: An offer-architecture case study: Version 1 had the highest AOV option at $60 (4 products + free gift, no spend-more incentive); Version 2 (photo) lifted AOV by $20 with roughly the same CVR while sending FEWER items to the customer. The takeaway is in the bundle structure, not the discount.
cta: none visible (photo of the Version 2 offer).
idea: AOV can rise $20 with flat CVR and fewer items shipped — the bundle architecture, not the discount, is the lever.
sequencing: Result: +$20 AOV, same CVR, fewer items.
Version 1: $60 top option, 4 products + gift, no incentive to spend more.
Version 2: the restructured offer (photo).
Implied lesson: architecture > discount.
formatting: Short case post + offer screenshot photo. Before/after structure.
why_it_works: "Same CVR, fewer items, +$20" is a paradox that forces the read — it breaks the assumption that AOV gains cost conversion or margin.
what_to_steal: The exact test for LC: restructure the bundle picker so the top tier is irresistible on value-perception while shipping fewer pieces — AOV up, COGS down, CVR flat.
